description: Hand-written extraction gold labels over fictional report prose. Each label records the exact source sentence so the label can be checked against the file rather than trusted. A claim may omit `sentence`, in which case it is the enclosing sentence.
howItWasLabelled: By reading each sentence in each document and recording what it unambiguously states. Labels were never derived from running an extractor, from a model's output, or from what any pipeline returned. A relation is labelled only when both arguments are identifiable within the sentence or the immediately preceding sentence of the same paragraph. Where a sentence states a relation that the 28-predicate vocabulary cannot express, or states one that is denied, hedged, irrelevant, or out of the organisation-to-organisation domain the vocabulary models, the label is `expectNothing` with a reason. Those negative labels are the point: an extractor that invents a relation for every sentence scores badly on them.
limitations: This is 10 documents and roughly fifty sentences. It is NOT a statistically representative sample of prose and must never be reported as one.

It is fictional prose written for this purpose. It exercises pronouns, multi-clause sentences, passive voice, negation, hedging, temporal statements, several relations per sentence, and instruction-shaped text. It does not exercise OCR noise, tables, or badly-scanned input.
Entity names are short and consistent by design. Real corpora with homonyms, aliases and transliteration variants are harder, and this set will overstate performance on those.
Predicates are constrained to the 28 registered relations, so this measures recall within that vocabulary only.
